title: Signal Trace
intent: Compare two observations, protect civilian radios and identify one armed carrier.
observed: The opening and inspection views closely repeat Market Lifeline's wrecked boulevard. Radio use and the two observation locations are not expressed strongly through scenery; a player sees trucks and scattered soldiers before seeing an investigation setting.
camera: Begin with the friendly observation group and first inspectable point. Offer a camera-only comparison of the two points, retaining visual context rather than zooming into anonymous vehicles.
light: Use consistent daylight so identification relies on silhouettes and authored evidence, not enemies artificially highlighted by lighting.
ground: Give each observation point a small, grounded standing area connected to existing pavement. Finish the damaged-road and curb interfaces inherited from the shared corridor.
props: Add a civilian radio repair counter, rooftop domestic antennas and small receiver/recording kits at the actual observation points. Keep the confirmed hostile device distinct only when the mission reveals it; avoid decorative cues that prematurely identify the suspect.
landscape: Reduce incidental tree/rock competition near the observation positions; preserve domestic courtyards and existing sight lines.

title: Safehouse Sweep
intent: Recognise two safehouse exits, occupied family homes and a courier/evidence objective.
observed: The same highway, trucks and wrecks dominate again. The reviewed views do not communicate an enclosed safehouse with two useful exits; protected homes visually merge with generic residential rubble.
camera: Shift mission guidance toward the verified house frontage and exits. Use a tactical angle where a roof does not hide both entrances; verify this against the actual exit anchors before changing the framing.
light: Preserve readable doorway recesses without turning the family homes into dark silhouettes. Subtle awning and facade contrast can separate entrances from walls.
ground: Use continuous doorstep paving and short courtyard paths to connect the two exits to the existing street. Preserve legal route widths and avoid visually implying an inaccessible passage.
props: Dress protected occupied homes with domestic water, laundry and food-storage details; reserve shutters, controlled entry and verified equipment cues for the actual safehouse. Add a grounded ledger/courier handoff point rather than arbitrary roadside crates.
landscape: Consolidate rubble at damaged building bases and leave occupied frontages maintained, making the inhabited-versus-damaged distinction intentional.

title: False Front
intent: Contrast an unconfirmed depot report with a real civilian evacuation and a later verified ambush.
observed: The native views are nearly indistinguishable from Signal Trace and Safehouse Sweep. The depot, exposed crossing and evacuation destination need a more coherent visual relationship; evenly distributed roadside wrecks dilute the specific threat.
camera: Show civilian vehicles and the next safe route segment first. Frame the unconfirmed depot as context without making it look like an already approved target.
light: Keep the depot visually neutral before verification. Build tension through occlusion and composition, while preserving civilian vehicle readability.
ground: Differentiate a maintained evacuation track from damaged roadside margins using coherent patches and tyre paths. Repair sudden sidewalk endings and avoid decorative rubble in actual escape lanes.
props: Use a plausible neutral depot loading front, an organised civilian assembly point and a restrained ambush position after confirmation. Add travel luggage or aid crates at the destination, not military props throughout every civilian space.
landscape: Use existing rock/terrain edges to frame the exposed road; reduce repeated isolated boulders and giant empty sand gaps around the mission's active area.
